root_cause: ptrace_syscallreq() range-checked the requested system call number with `sv_size < code` (an off-by-one that lets code == sv_size pass) and did so before resolving the syscall(2)/__syscall(2) indirection, which replaces the number with args[0] that was never range-checked, and it shifted the argument array by ts_nargs - 1 without requiring ts_nargs > 0; the fix checks `sc >= sv_size` after the indirection and rejects indirect calls with zero arguments.
notes: Fix commit is on stable/15 (Approved by: so); the main-branch hash was not confirmed. Commit message: Fixes: 140ceb5d956b (ptrace(2): add PT_SC_REMOTE remote syscall request). The request is built from the debugger's arguments in sys/kern/sys_process.c and run by the traced thread in kern_sig.c. One fix closes three defects (off-by-one, check before indirection, nargs underflow); the judgment treats the check-before-indirection defect as the main one. Regression tests added in tests/sys/kern/ptrace_test.c. Affects 14.3, 14.4 and 15.0.

root_cause: exec_args_adjust_args() computed the memmove length for shifting the strings already in the execve argument buffer as `args->endp - args->begin_argv + consume` instead of `args->endp - (args->begin_argv + consume)` (an operator-precedence error), so the move copied 2*consume bytes more than the used area and could overwrite adjacent execve argument regions.
notes: Fix commit is on stable/15 (Approved by: so); the main-branch hash was not confirmed. Commit message: Fixes: f373437a01a3 (Add helper functions to copy strings into struct image_args); it says userspace could overflow the copy into adjacent execve KVA regions. One-line fix. Affects 13.5, 14.3, 14.4 and 15.0.

component: FreeBSD kernel credential helper used by mac_do(4) (FreeBSD-SA-26:59.mac_do)
root_cause: After commit be1f7435ef21 moved the effective group ID out of cr_groups[0] into its own cr_gid field, group_is_primary() in sys/ucred.h still compared against cr_groups[0], which now holds the first supplementary group or, for a credential with no supplementary groups, a zeroed unused slot (gid 0), so mac_do(4), its only user, treated gid 0 as the caller's primary group when deciding whether a setcred(2) transition keeps the caller's primary groups.
notes: FreeBSD 15 only (the credential layout change landed in 15.0). Fix commit is on stable/15 (Approved by: so); the main-branch hash was not confirmed. Commit message: Fixes: be1f7435ef21 (kern: start tracking cr_gid outside of cr_groups[]); ucreds are allocated with M_ZERO, so the unused slot reads as 0. Regression test added under tests/sys/mac/do. The caller is in sys/security/mac_do/mac_do.c (the commit says mac_do is the only user; the call site itself was not read).

root_cause: nfsrpc_readdir() and nfsrpc_readdirplus() passed file names from the NFS server's READDIR reply into directory entries without rejecting names that contain '/' or NUL (or, for NFSv4, the names '.' and '..', which the client makes itself); the NFS RFCs allow such characters but POSIX names cannot hold them, so a malicious server made readdir(3) return entries with extra path components; the fix adds nfscl_invalidfname() and skips such entries.
notes: 026cdaa3 is the main commit (from the cherry-pick line of stable/14 commit 9328ded386d5). The impact is a confused deputy: programs that copy files from an NFS mount can be led outside the source or destination directory. OpenBSD fixed the same class in its readdir path (7.4 errata 022); that fix is not used here.

component: FreeBSD pf(4) ICMP and ICMPv6 state tracking (FreeBSD-SA-24:05.pf)
root_cause: pf built the state key for ICMP and ICMPv6 from the ICMP identifier alone, placed in both port slots with no message type or query/reply direction, and used 0 for messages that carry no identifier such as Neighbor Discovery, so an ICMPv6 Echo Request with identifier 0 matched the state created by a Neighbor Solicitation and passed without rule evaluation; the fix, imported from OpenBSD, puts the ICMP type mapped by pf_icmp_mapping() into one port of the key.
notes: The fix is a series on stable/14: 370e196bae46 (stricter state checking for ICMP and ICMPv6, cherry-picked from main 534ee17e61ee and 2f6b4611b5b8, which carry the same title), then c95f99c, 6979b4d and 3382c691dc6a (allow MLD LR to be sent without state), which is the hash the advisory lists. Later commits in September 2024 (fb925cf to 1e965d5 on releng/14.1) repaired regressions of the series. vulnerable_ref and fixed_ref are on stable/14. The advisory condition: rules that allow ND and block incoming Echo Requests.

component: FreeBSD jails, unix socket SCM_RIGHTS descriptor passing (FreeBSD-SA-26:04.jail)
root_cause: Jail filesystem confinement was enforced only during path lookup (a lookup may not climb above the jail root), and descriptors received over a unix socket from a process in a jail with a different root were installed into the receiver with no restriction, so a jailed process could receive a directory outside its own root and look up paths or fchdir from it; the fix marks every descriptor that crosses a jail boundary with FD_RESOLVE_BENEATH so lookups through it cannot leave that directory.
notes: Main commit 350ba9672a7f (unix: Set O_RESOLVE_BENEATH on fds transferred between jails, PR 262179); stable/14 commit 3ad3ab5f9b6e. The advisory patch also carries the FD_RESOLVE_BENEATH infrastructure (fcntl flag, fget_cap flags, vfs_cache.c) from earlier commits whose hashes were not identified. The fix adds restrict_rights() in uipc_usrreq.c; unp_externalize is named from the commit message (the SCM_RIGHTS externalize path), its exact call site was not read. Needs two jails with different roots that can share a unix socket (for example through a shared nullfs mount).

root_cause: nmreq_copyin() walked the user-space option list once with copyin to compute the size of the kernel buffer, then walked it again with a second copyin and trusted the option sizes read the second time without checking them against the size computed in the first pass, so a thread that changed the options between the passes corrupted kernel memory; the fix sizes the buffer for the largest allowed request and checks each option size during the copying pass.
notes: 393729916564 is the main commit (from the cherry-pick line of stable/13 commit 9f600a260a73). The same advisory patch also fixes CVE-2022-23085 (an option size that could overflow); that CVE is not used as a separate sample. Reachable from a jail only when netmap is in the jail's devfs ruleset.

component: Apple XNU virtual memory, named memory entries (kfd 'PhysPuppet')
root_cause: mach_memory_object_memory_entry_64() stored the caller's unaligned size in the named entry while the backing VM object was rounded up to whole pages, vm_map_enter_mem_object_helper() passed the unaligned size on to vm_map_enter(), and the page-alignment checks on the unmap path (vm_map_delete, pmap_remove_options) existed only under MACH_ASSERT in debug and development builds, so release kernels shifted away the unaligned tail in pmap_remove_options_internal() and left one page-table entry mapping a page that was then freed.
notes: Apple publishes source tarballs per release, not fix commits. Fixed in iOS 16.4 and macOS 13.3 per the kfd writeup; the XNU source tag of the first fixed release was not confirmed, so fixed_ref is null (a re-tester can diff the next tag after xnu-8792.81.2). The root cause and file paths come from the kfd writeup; the exact lines Apple changed are unknown. The pmap part is in the arm pmap, so the unmap-side effect is specific to arm64 devices. Apple's security notes were not read.

classes: Consistency across sibling branches and similar entry points
root_cause: In pledge_ioctl() the TIOCUCNTL case tested whether the descriptor was a pty master by reading vp->v_rdev without first checking that the file is a vnode (fp->f_type == DTYPE_VNODE) and that the vnode is a character device (vp->v_type == VCHR), checks that sibling cases in the same switch such as BIOCGSTATS make, so calling TIOCUCNTL on a non-file descriptor from a pledged process crashed the kernel.
notes: No CVE. OpenBSD calls it a reliability fix (released 2025-07-01); the impact is a local kernel crash. The errata patch applies to sys/kern/kern_pledge.c CVS revision 1.320 as shipped in OpenBSD 7.6; the GitHub mirror has no release tags or branches, and the git hash of the -current fix was not found, so both refs are null. A search result says OpenBSD 7.7 errata 008 carries the same fix (not read).

component: Microsoft Windows tcpip.sys IPv6 extension header handling
root_cause: Ipv6pProcessOptions(), which checks the options of one packet, reported an option error through IppSendErrorList(), which acts on every packet of the coalesced chain and changes their state (the analyses describe the packet size or next-header field being reset), so other packets of the chain that were never examined went on into fragment handling, where Ipv6pReceiveFragment() subtracted the header length from the changed size without a check and reassembly copied more than it allocated; the August 2024 patch calls IppSendError() for the single packet instead.
notes: Closed source: question-level test only. The patch-level change (IppSendErrorList replaced by IppSendError in Ipv6pProcessOptions, behind a feature flag) comes from public binary diffs of tcpip.sys; the two analyses read disagree on which per-packet field is reset. The MalwareTech and BI.ZONE analyses exist but returned HTTP 403 and were not read; the MSRC advisory was not read. Remote, pre-authentication, IPv6 only.
